name: Kain, Traitorous Dragoon
description: As long as it's your turn, this creature has flying. Whenever this creature deals combat damage to a player, that player gains control of it. You draw cards equal to the damage dealt, create that many tapped Treasure tokens, and lose that much life.
assumptions: Read node:jump as "As long as it's your turn, this creature has flying."

Read node:controlChange (becomes, owner:any, no zone change, player=damagedPlayer) as a control-change effect — the becomes role is defined for identity/type changes, not explicitly control changes, so this reading is inferred.
Assumed draw/Treasure/life-loss print in flow.steps order and still belong to the original controller despite the intervening control change.
couldNotDerive: The ability's own name ("Jump") — not encoded anywhere, same as other named abilities on other cards.
notes: Agent misinterpretation, not a decomposition gap — corrected after initial misjudgment. Real oracle text reads "...that player gains control of Kain. If they do, you draw..." I first evaluated node:controlChange's own `to` field (bf, not stack) in isolation and called this a missing contingency concept. Wrong: controlChange (and draw/treasure/lifeLoss nested under it) already sits under node:onDealsDamage, which IS to:"stack" — so the whole chain is already contingent on that trigger resolving, per our own rule. That's exactly what "if they do" is describing: if Kain is removed from the battlefield in response to the trigger being on the stack, the control-change clause (and everything after it) simply can't happen. The data already models this correctly; the reconstruction just didn't render the nuance into text. No schema/decomposition fix needed. Missing the ability's own name ("Jump") is expected and not counted — same category as other unencoded ability names elsewhere (e.g. Malboro's "Bad Breath").
